function: Learned codebook-index prediction for distributed beamforming among four LEO satellites, maximizing the achievable rate at one terrestrial user (p. 7).
system: p. 3, 8: LEO satellites with M = 4/8/16/32 transmit antennas, user with K receive antennas, four satellites at 750 km, 10 GHz, 10 MHz; no RIS.
method: p. 5-7: ResNet-18 supervised classifier of the optimal codebook index, trained with semi-synchronous federated learning (weighted aggregation at a server satellite); transfer learning only as future work.
data_channel: p. 4-5: custom simulation: STK orbit distances, shadowed Rician small-scale fading generated in MATLAB, large-scale loss with exponent 2; no 3GPP model, no measurements.
test_conditions: p. 5-10: trained on simulated data per satellite; local and server test sets not described as a new scenario; sweeps of antennas, satellites, altitude, CSI error.
baselines: p. 9-10: non-learned ideal beamforming (IB) and single-satellite network at 43/46/49 dBm; learned MLP, LSTM, and CNN benchmarks (Fig. 15).
metrics: p. 8-10: achievable rate (bits), global testing accuracy, training loss, versus time slot, antennas, satellites, altitude.
q1_support: p. 5: "The small-scale fading coefficients are generated by MATLAB according to the Rician distributions." The channel is a custom shadowed Rician model (p. 4); no 3GPP TR 38.811 or 38.901 model, DeepMIMO, or measured data is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 6: "there are two possible future directions, where transfer learning can be employed". Training data come from the simulator (p. 5) and the server test set (p. 7) is not described as another scenario; sweeps over antennas, satellites, altitude and CSI error (pp. 8-10) report no train-test mismatch.
q3_support: p. 10: "The multilayer perception (MLP) [45], long-short term memory (LSTM) [46] and convolutional neural networks (CNN) are evaluated as benchmark schemes." p. 9: "A single satellite scenario with different transmit power is considered as a benchmark scheme." Ideal beamforming also compared; all on achievable rate (Figs. 9, 10, 15).
q4_support: p. 4: "a low-complexity codebook-based precoding matrix is designed" is only qualitative; no order of complexity, operations, parameter count, or runtime is reported for ResNet-18 or the FederSat scheme.
q5_support: p. 5: "the training dataset are generated by the simulation softwares" (STK and MATLAB); no code or data link, public dataset, or measured data is given.
notes: Title and DOI match on p. 1. Area 6: learned beam (codebook) control of LEO satellite links. Area 7 does not apply because the server satellite decodes and demodulates the uploaded models (p. 6), so aggregation is digital, and the problem solved is beamforming. RIS appears only in related work (pp. 1-2). q2 is 0 although p. 7 says the server test set is a 'broader or entirely different dataset' and claims generalization 'when parameters vary': no new scenario is described or reported separately, and the antenna, satellite, altitude and CSI sweeps look like separate runs or error sweeps. q3 relies on MLP, LSTM and CNN as standard architectures for the same problem, plus ideal beamforming and the single-satellite network as non-learned benchmarks.
